built.summary:
I1 (backend money guards and storefront tip) is done. The gift-card and loyalty paths can no longer move a bill while the card machine is charging it. The storefront writes tip_cents in the order insert. The postRefundPayment cancelled-branch item is not_needed: no production code reaches it.

(a) Card-machine guard:
- `giftCards/service.ts` `redeemGiftCardTx` calls `assertNoActiveTerminalChargeTx` right after its order `FOR UPDATE`. It uses a static import: `connectors/terminal/guard.ts` imports only `lib/prisma` and `lib/errors`, so there is no import cycle.
- `loyalty/service.ts`: `adjustOrderBill` now runs in one transaction (`adjustOrderBillTx`). It locks the order row, calls the guard, then moves the total and the pending rows. The guard applies both ways: lowering the bill, and the storefront's put-back that raises it.
- `redeemPointsOnOrder` is one transaction:
  - lock the order row;
  - read status, owner and paid payments under the lock (404 / ORDER_NOT_OPEN);
  - call the guard;
  - check ALREADY_REDEEMED under the lock;
  - quote, claim the points and lower the bill;
  - book the redeem after commit.
- Two concurrent redeems on one order used to be able to both pass; now exactly one does.
- The discount is now capped at what is still owed (total minus paid), the same as gift cards. A paid-up order gives 422 NOTHING_DUE.
- `claimRedemption` (storefront) now also takes the order lock before the loyalty-account row. It is not guarded, because it only raises discountCents and never moves the bill.
- Lock order is order row first, then everything else, matching every till caller. A test runs a gift card and a points redeem on one order at once; both apply and there is no deadlock.

(b) Storefront tip: `OrderDTO` (`_types/order.ts`) now has `tip_cents?: number`. In `storefront/routes.ts` I removed `tipInInsert` and the later `orderPatch.tipCents` write; the DTO now sends `tip_cents: body.tipCents`. The ingestOrder ceiling (payment.amountCents + wallet_amount_cents) always holds the tip:
- With a wallet top-up, the tip stays inside payment.amountCents.
- With the wallet as the method, the wallet share covers the tip.

(c) postRefundPayment cancelled branch: not_needed. `writeRefundTx` (pos/service) is the only code that writes refund Payment rows:
- `refundOrder` sends every cancelled or rejected ticket to `refundDueOnCancelledTicket`, which books through `bookCancelledHandBackTx` (the R5-A/B/C-correct unwind), never through postRefundPayment.
- The TILL-R3 void path calls `assertVoidable` under the order lock, so it only runs on open orders.
- No script or backfill calls postRefundPayment.

The branch is reachable only by calling postRefundPayment directly, which `auditLedgerFollowups` does for the simple case (drawer closes after the cancel), where its Dr 1110 / Cr drawer entry is correct. No test can show a production failure. Changing it to refuse would break that test. Making it delegate would need orderPosting to import pos/service, which is a cycle. So `orderPosting.ts` is unchanged.

items.note: W4-MONEY-1 item 3. redeemGiftCardTx: guard right after the order FOR UPDATE, via a static import (no cycle: guard.ts imports only lib/prisma and lib/errors). loyalty: adjustOrderBill and redeemPointsOnOrder lower or raise the bill only inside a transaction that locks the order row first and then calls assertNoActiveTerminalChargeTx. On a refusal: 409 TERMINAL_CHARGE_ACTIVE {chargeId}, and the points, discount, card and bill are all unchanged. claimRedemption also takes the order lock first, so the lock order matches the till. Extras that came out of the locked transaction: redeemPointsOnOrder is race-free (one ALREADY_REDEEMED); the discount is capped at what is still owed (new 422 NOTHING_DUE when nothing is owed).

Last bullet only (the other optional bullets belong to other streams): _types/order.ts OrderDTO now has tip_cents?: number; the tipInInsert fallback and the post-insert orderPatch.tipCents write are removed from storefront/routes.ts; the insert always sends tip_cents: body.tipCents. This is consistent with ingestOrder's ceiling (payment + wallet share).

Same change as item 9. A test proves a wallet-as-method checkout with a PKR 100 tip stores tipCents=10,000 with total 0. Another proves ingestOrder takes a tip up to payment + wallet and refuses more (INVALID_TIP).

review.title: redeemPointsOnOrder holds an interactive transaction (and the order row lock) while quoteRedemption runs queries on the global pool, so P concurrent customer redeems can tie up the whole API connection pool and all fail
review.scenario: redeemPointsOnOrder (around lines 425-460) now opens prisma.$transaction, which takes one pool connection, and takes the order FOR UPDATE lock. Inside that transaction it calls quoteRedemption (lines 276-301). quoteRedemption runs loyaltyAccountOf(), and loadLoyaltySettings() on a cache miss, through the global `prisma` client rather than `tx`, so each call needs a second pool connection. With a pool of P connections (Prisma's default is num_cpus*2+1, and no connection_limit is set anywhere in the repo), P simultaneous POST /loyalty/redeem calls each hold one connection and wait for another that never frees up. Every one fails after the 5 s interactive-transaction timeout with 'Transaction already closed', and for those 5 s every other API request, for every company, waits on the pool. One signed-in customer with one open order can cause this: fire P parallel redeems, and the extra requests also hold connections while they queue on the order lock. Reproduced on DB servd_test_i1_rv with ?connection_limit=3. A scratchpad probe calls redeemPointsOnOrder on different orders, each customer holding 5,000 points. 2 concurrent: both succeed in 92 ms. 3 concurrent: all 3 fail after 5,028 ms with 'Transaction API error: Transaction already closed ... expired transaction'. Before this change the redeem was not one long transaction, so it could not starve itself. The storefront claimRedemption and the gift-card paths are fine: they only use `tx`.
review.fix: Keep every read in redeemPointsOnOrder on `tx`. Option 1: give quoteRedemption an optional `db: Tx | typeof prisma = prisma` and read the account with `db.loyaltyAccount.findUnique({ where: { tenantId_customerId: { tenantId, customerId } } })`; redeemPointsOnOrder passes `tx`. Also warm the settings before the transaction opens: read the order's concept.tenantId unlocked, call `await loadLoyaltySettings(tenantId)` (cached for its TTL), then open the transaction and re-check the tenant under the lock. Option 2: call quoteRedemption before the transaction with capCents = total − paid, then inside the locked transaction re-read the outstanding amount and re-cap with `Math.min(quote.discountCents, outstanding)` and `points = ceil(discount / value)`. claimRedemptionTx's conditional decrement already guards the balance. Optionally pass `{ maxWait, timeout }` as applyGiftCardTender does. Add a regression test that sets connection_limit=N and runs N concurrent redeems, expecting all to succeed.

fix.summary:
I1-RV-1 is real and now fixed. Before the fix I reproduced it. With connection_limit=3 and 3 redeems running at once, all 3 failed after about 5,030 ms with "Transaction already closed". The cause: redeemPointsOnOrder opened an interactive transaction (one pool connection plus the order row lock), then quoteRedemption read the loyalty account through loyaltyAccountOf, and the settings through loadLoyaltySettings and calculatePointsValue, on the global client. Each of those reads needed a second pool connection.

Fix, in /home/user/servd/backend/src/modules/loyalty/service.ts:
(1) quoteRedemption's logic moved into a private quoteWith(settings, args, readBalance). It takes settings already loaded and a balance reader from the caller. The discount is usable × point value, the same as calculatePointsValue, so that import is gone. The public quoteRedemption keeps its signature and behaviour; the storefront checkout still calls it outside any transaction.
(2) Before the transaction opens, redeemPointsOnOrder now reads the order's company without a lock (same where clause, so a foreign or missing order is still 404) and loads that company's loyalty settings.
(3) Inside the transaction every read goes through tx, including the balance (tx.loyaltyAccount.findUnique on (tenantId, customerId)). Under the lock it checks the order's company again; if it changed it returns a new 409 ORDER_CHANGED and never quotes on another company's settings.
(4) The transaction now passes { maxWait: 10_000, timeout: 15_000 }, as the orders and checkSplit transactions do.
(5) The final newBalance read happens after commit, as before.

Lock order (order row, then loyalty account), once-per-order, the terminal-charge 409, the cap at what is still owed, and per-company points are all unchanged.

items.note: Confirmed before the fix: at connection_limit=3, 3 concurrent redeems all failed at about 5 s. Took a mix of options 1 and 2: the settings and the order's company are read before the transaction, every read inside it is on tx (balance via a tx reader passed to the new quoteWith), and the company is re-checked under the lock (409 ORDER_CHANGED). Added maxWait/timeout. Regression test in tests/integrationMoney.test.ts runs a child tsx process with connection_limit=3, a cold settings cache and 3 concurrent redeems on separate orders. It expects all 3 to succeed in under 5 s, each customer to have 4,000 points left and each bill to be 90,000 with a 10,000 discount. It failed before the fix and passes after.

fix.tests: Ran on a scratch DB, servd_test_i1_fix, which is now dropped. The new regression test failed before the fix with the exact 'Transaction already closed ... 5000 ms' error. After the fix, all 23 test files that mention loyalty or redeem pass: 23 files, 354 tests, including integrationMoney (12), loyalty, auditLedgerLoyalty, auditMoneyFollowups, auditOnlineCheckout and auditTillGiftCard. `tsc --noEmit` reports no errors in the changed files. I did not run the full suite.
fix.prodNotes: POST /loyalty/redeem can now return a new error, 409 ORDER_CHANGED, but only if the order's brand changes company between the unlocked read and the lock, which should never happen in practice. The redeem transaction now allows up to 10 s to get a connection and 15 s to run, up from Prisma's defaults of 2 s and 5 s. Prod sets no connection_limit, so the pool is Prisma's default (num_cpus*2+1). Before this fix that many concurrent redeems would block the whole API.

review.title: The `targetPaymentId` doc comment says it is null on a sale charge, but split-bill sale charges carry the portion's payment id
review.scenario:
TerminalChargeView.targetPaymentId (service.ts:145) is documented as "A refund charge: the card payment it refunds (null on a sale charge)", and the builder's summary repeats this. But startTerminalCharge (service.ts:327) writes `targetPaymentId: input.paymentId ?? null` on kind 'charge', and recordCharge (:567) settles that payment.

So a card-portion charge on a split bill returns `kind: 'charge', targetPaymentId: <split payment id>`. The one consumer today, refundEngine.inFlightRefundFor, filters on kind === 'refund' first, so nothing breaks now. A future consumer that trusts the comment and uses `targetPaymentId != null` as the test for 'is a refund' would treat a split-bill sale as a refund in flight and block refunds on that payment.
review.fix: Change the comment at service.ts:145 to: "The payment this charge settles (a split-bill card portion) or refunds (kind 'refund'); null on a whole-order sale charge." Also update the matching comment in frontend/admin/src/components/pos/tillApi.ts:481.

The only file I changed was backend/src/connectors/terminal/service.ts, where I rewrote the TerminalChargeView.targetPaymentId doc comment. It now says the field is the payment the charge settles (split-bill card portion, kind 'charge') or refunds (kind 'refund'), and is null on a whole-order sale charge. It also says to tell a refund by kind === 'refund', never by targetPaymentId != null. This is a comment-only change with no behaviour change.
